summary: This bill amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to bar housing providers from obtaining or using any consumer credit report to screen tenants for rental approval, security deposits, lease terms, or retention, even with the tenant's consent except for individualized reconsideration after an initial denial.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to prohibit credit checks in tenant screening. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address health insurance, medical care delivery, or healthcare markets.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, background checks for guns, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill pertains to immigration status, visas, border policy, or pathways to residency.
The bill does not address reproductive healthcare, abortion access, or related regulations.
No references to defense spending, military policy, or national security appropriations.
The bill contains no environmental, energy, or climate-related provisions.

While the bill may indirectly affect housing access for lower-income individuals by limiting credit screening, it does not modify any welfare programs, eligibility rules, or benefit levels such as SNAP, TANF, or housing vouchers.
No provisions relate to schools, student aid, school choice, or education funding.
The bill does not address controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
Nothing in the text concerns sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
The legislation has no bearing on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No fiscal provisions affect deficits, debt ceiling, or debt reduction measures.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights specific to LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions involve foreign assistance, international aid, or State Department funding.
The bill contains no election administration, voting access, or campaign finance measures.

Although the bill restricts use of consumer reports (a form of data), it is narrowly focused on rental housing decisions under the FCRA and does not engage broader technology regulation, data privacy frameworks, or platform oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, wages, or workplace regulations.
The bill does not involve religious exemptions, anti-discrimination laws, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
